title: AE/CSM 1:1 prep — Account Nimbus (scratchpad)
content:
Meeting context:
- Who: Sofia (CSM) + Noah Blake (AE) 1:1 prep ahead of Tue 2026-03-12 customer sync (pre-call internal runthrough).
- Account: Nimbus (marketing automation platform). On Redwood Dedicated trial; pilot uses r/w embeddings + low-latency chat. Renewal decision Q2. ARR ~ $120k potential.
- Why this call matters: technical latency complaints + licensing conversation upcoming. Want to align AE/CSM approach so we don’t scare them with price early.

Top objective for my 1:1 with Noah:
1) Align on messaging for technical issues -> how we surface timeline for fixes without overpromising.
2) Agree next steps on renewal cadence and who owns which outreach.
3) Confirm ask list for SE to bring to next customer call (quantization plan + perf SLA).

Quick account health snapshot (notes to self):
- Tech: two customers reported 95th percentile token latency spikes on long prompts (>1024). SE lab suspects KV cache warmup + batch config.
- Usage: steady growth last 3 weeks; token spend up 28% MoM. Burst pattern afternoons PST.
- Billing: on pilot credits, internal finance flagged potential overrun if production set.
- Exec sponsor: Emily Tran (VP Product) engaged but prefers consolidated technical answers.

Agenda items to propose internally with AE before customer call:
- 5m: recap of current incidents + temporary mitigation (prefix caching tweak).
- 10m: SE summary of root cause and timeline for SDK patch (target: 2 weeks).
- 8m: Commercial ask framing — soft probe on topline budget window for next quarter.
- 5m: Decide on trial extension vs upgrade ask.

Questions to confirm with Noah (do in 1:1):
- Is AE comfortable with saying "we're prioritizing a patch in 2 weeks" vs "investigating"? (I lean toward specific if SE confirms schedule).
- Who will own the renewal email to Emily? (Noah offered to draft but we should coordinate tone.)
- Are we okay to surface a potential price band if they request guaranteed lower latency SLA? (Pre-approve with RevOps?).

Draft talking points for customer (short):
- Acknowledge their latency spikes and outline immediate mitigation we applied.
- High-level cause (cache/ batching interplay) + concrete ETA for the SDK/runtime patch.
- Offer temporary configuration change we can apply live after call (low-friction).
- Discuss renewal windows and options: Dedicated reserved vs staged Dedicated + burst credits.

Action items (owner / due):
- SE (Jordan Kim): run full repro with 2k token context + produce perf comparison of current runtime vs patched kernel. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Sofia: prepare short one-pager (2 slides) summarizing issue + mitigation to send to Emily ahead of next customer touchpoint. Due: 2026-03-13 (send by EOD).
- Noah (AE): draft renewal outreach email proposing a 30-day pilot extension and tentative commercial band. Due: 2026-03-14.
- Ravi (Solutions SE): prepare recommended config snippet that we can toggle immediately (low-risk). Due: 2026-03-12 (before customer sync).
- Finance/RevOps (Elena Ruiz): prepare two pricing scenarios for Dedicated commit (12-month vs 6-month) with estimated unit token price and overage protection. Due: 2026-03-17.

Risks / escalation notes (to mention quietly in 1:1):
- If patch slips >3 weeks, risk of exec churn increases. Need a contingency messaging plan.
- Billing surprise: if usage keeps spiking and we don’t present options, customer may postpone renewal.

Notes-to-self / things to bring up quickly:
- Ask Noah if he’s seen the latest customer feedback thread in #cs-nimbus (there's a buried note about feature gating that might change their timeline).
- Confirm whether we can offer a one-off credit to reduce friction — coordinate with RevOps before making promises.
- Keep language non-technical on exec update; have SE bullet points for follow-ups.

Backlog items (not for this call):
- Build eval test for 95th percentile latency under multi-user burst for Nimbus workload sim. (Assign to SRE later).
- Follow-up on enabling extended logging for first 48h after patch.

Final quick prep checklist for 1:1 (Sofia):
- [x] Review SE replication notes (Jordan).
- [x] Pull last 14 days token usage + cost trend.
- [ ] Draft the one-pager (target tonight).
- [ ] Confirm Noah's draft email before sending.

Open questions I want answered in the 1:1:
- Which commercial scenario is Noah leaning to: soft extension vs immediate commit?
- If we offer a credit, what internal approvals needed and how fast?

End of scratchpad — will tidy and move key lines to customer-facing doc once Noah and Jordan confirm timelines.
